task.description: Perform WF-02 Step 1b (design gate, hard gate) for REQ-373 per docs/agents/workflows/WF-02_requirement_implementation.md and your own role file .claude/agents/code-design-validator.md. Read lib/letflow/design/req373-service-catalog-version-lifecycle.md INDEPENDENTLY and in full -- do not read CODE-DESIGNER's handoff result.summary as a substitute for reading the actual design doc. For each of REQ-373's 8 acceptance criteria (in task.acceptance_criteria below), verify it has a corresponding, unambiguous design element (no TBD/deferral). Verify: function signatures fully specified (name, inputs, outputs, error cases); error handling shape stated; cross-module dependencies listed; NO implementation code present anywhere in the doc (no literal .ex code blocks with function bodies, case/do/end blocks, or literal clause implementations -- signatures and type shapes only). Specifically check the design's own flagged issues: (1) the schema-decision reasoning (in-place columns + sibling table vs. composite key) is sound and doesn't silently break any of service_catalog.ex's 5 existing public functions; (2) AC4's retire-vs-fallback ambiguity is genuinely resolved, not left implicit; (3) the PinResolver.Lookup behaviour callback contract is correctly understood and correctly designed against (re-read lib/letflow/engine/pin_resolver.ex yourself to confirm, don't trust the design doc's own claim about it); (4) publish/retire route/permission design correctly reuses the existing :AdminServicesManage permission by name, not inventing one. FAIL immediately on any check failure -- no partial credit. Set this handoff's status to COMPLETED and fill result with your genuine independent verdict; commit and push the handoff to git before ending your turn.
acceptance_criteria: service_catalog entries carry a version identity and an ACTIVE/RETIRED status, with the chosen schema (composite key vs. status+sibling table) stated explicitly in the moduledoc along with the reasoning, proven by a migration and a schema test

publishing a new version of an existing service_id does not alter or invalidate any already-resolved pinned_version entry recorded in a prior INSTANCE_STARTED event, proven by a test that resolves a pin, publishes a new version, and re-derives the same instance's effective pin set unchanged
a new case created after a publish resolves the newly published version via Letflow.Engine.PinResolver.resolve/4's real (non-default) Lookup, proven by a test

retiring a version prevents any NEW resolution from choosing it (a fresh resolve/4 call against the retired ref fails or falls through to the current version, whichever this requirement's own design specifies -- stated explicitly, not left ambiguous) while an instance already pinned to the retired version continues to resolve via pin_for/3 with no error, proven by a test covering both sides

Engine.create/2's pin_lookup/2 helper is wired to the real catalog-backed Lookup for catalog_entry references in place of PinResolver.default_lookup/0, proven by an integration test that starts a real instance referencing a SERVICE_TASK's service_id and confirms a :resolved (not :unresolved_catalog_ref-failing) pin is recorded
publish/retire operations are gated behind the already-shipped :AdminServicesManage permission (Letflow.Api.Authorization), not a newly invented permission name, proven by a test

PLC-01/module_ref catalog versioning is explicitly named as still out of scope in the moduledoc, with a citation of pin_resolver.ex's own existing SCOPE GAP language, not silently expanded into this requirement's scope
mix letflow.check passes, with real output quoted

checks_passed: All 8 ACs have a mapped design element in §8 table; no TBD/deferral language found
No literal implementation code present -- the doc's one fenced code block (§0, lines 54-59) is a verbatim quote of EXISTING engine.ex source for re-verification, not new code

Schema-decision reasoning (§1: in-place columns + sibling table, not composite key) independently re-derived against pin_resolver.ex's actual Lookup.catalog_lookup contract (service_id alone, no version arg) -- sound, and correctly traced against service_catalog.ex's actual 5 core functions (register/1, get_for_tenant/2, list_for_tenant/2, update_scope/2, delete/1) plus list_all/1/scope_validator_lookup/1 -- all confirmed untouched in signature/arity/error-contract by reading service_catalog.ex and entry.ex directly

AC4 retire-vs-fallback ambiguity is genuinely resolved, not implicit: §3.2 states 'retire FAILS OUTRIGHT, never falls through' with an explicit structural reasoning paragraph, and separately names why pin_for/3 (already-pinned instances) is unaffected (structural: pin_for/3 never queries the catalog) -- verified against pin_resolver.ex's actual pin_for/3 body (pure Enum.find/2 over an in-memory list, zero Repo/Lookup calls)

PinResolver.Lookup contract correctly understood: re-read lib/letflow/engine/pin_resolver.ex directly -- Lookup is a plain struct (not an OTP behaviour), catalog_lookup :: (service_id -> {:ok, %{resolved_id, version}} | {:error, :not_found}), takes service_id alone. §5's catalog_lookup/1 spec and build/0's copy-default_lookup-for-module/variable_schema-fields description match this exactly.

Publish/retire route design reuses :AdminServicesManage by name, not a new permission -- verified directly in lib/letflow/api/authorization.ex: the existing prefix-match clause (lines 562-564, `endpoint_policy_key(method, "/admin/services" <> _rest) when method in ["POST","PATCH","DELETE"], do: :AdminServicesManage`) automatically covers both new POST routes with zero authorization.ex change, exactly as §0/§7 claim

checks_failed.defect: The new `status` field's representation is internally self-contradictory and never reconciled -- a genuine ambiguity, not a stylistic nit. §4's migration fixes the DB-level CHECK constraint and column default to UPPERCASE strings ('ACTIVE'/'RETIRED': `CHECK (status IN ('ACTIVE', 'RETIRED'))`, default `"ACTIVE"`), matching this codebase's own established convention for an uppercase-valued Ecto.Enum (required_auth: atoms :NONE/:API_KEY/:OAUTH2/:MUTUAL_TLS map by default Ecto.Enum behavior to identically-cased DB strings 'NONE'/'API_KEY'/... -- confirmed by reading entry.ex and the base migration directly). But §3.2's retire/1 behavior description ('status = :retired'), §3.2's already-retired guard ('status == :retired'), and §5's catalog_lookup/1 behavior ('row with status: :active ->', 'row with status: :retired ->') all repeatedly pattern-match on LOWERCASE atoms :active/:retired. Under this codebase's own default Ecto.Enum convention (atom's own casing becomes the DB string verbatim, as already true for both required_auth and scope), lowercase atoms :active/:retired would store as lowercase 'active'/'retired' -- directly contradicting §4's uppercase CHECK constraint and column default. The design never declares `status` as `Ecto.Enum` at all (unlike §0's own bullet, which explicitly annotates required_auth and scope as '(Ecto.Enum)' but conspicuously never does so for status), and never states a custom `values: [active: "ACTIVE", retired: "RETIRED"]` mapping that would reconcile lowercase-atom-in-code with uppercase-string-in-DB. This is not an open question CODE-DESIGNER flagged (absent from §9's OQ-1..OQ-4) -- it is an unflagged, load-bearing self-contradiction between two sections of the same document. It directly undermines AC1 ('ACTIVE/RETIRED status... schema... stated explicitly'), AC3 (catalog_lookup's ACTIVE-row match), and AC4 (retire's status-transition guard and the RETIRED-row match) -- an ELIXIR-DEV implementer following §5's literal prose (lowercase atoms) would ship a schema/CHECK-constraint mismatch or a changeset cast failure; one following §4's literal DB values would contradict §3.2/§5's own described pattern matches. Fix required: CODE-DESIGNER must pick one casing convention and state explicitly (a) whether `status` is `Ecto.Enum` on Entry's schema and (b) its exact `values:` mapping (plain `[:ACTIVE, :RETIRED]` to align with required_auth's own uppercase-atom convention, or an explicit `[active: "ACTIVE", retired: "RETIRED"]` mapping if lowercase atoms are intentionally preferred at the Elixir call-site level), then make every status literal in §3.2/§5/§8 consistent with that choice.

result.summary: FAIL. Independently re-verified §0's claims against service_catalog.ex, entry.ex, pin_resolver.ex, and authorization.ex directly (not the design's own self-report) -- the schema-decision reasoning, AC4 retire-vs-fallback resolution, PinResolver.Lookup contract usage, and permission reuse all check out correctly. However, the design leaves the new `status` column's Ecto representation unspecified and internally contradictory: the migration (§4) fixes uppercase DB values ('ACTIVE'/'RETIRED') while the behavior prose (§3.2, §5) repeatedly pattern-matches on lowercase atoms (:active/:retired), with no Ecto.Enum declaration or value-mapping anywhere reconciling the two. This is exactly the kind of implementation-blocking ambiguity the design gate exists to catch. Routing back to CODE-DESIGNER for rework -- do not have ELIXIR-DEV guess which casing is correct.
